children: Shares of network chips maker MACOM Technology Solutions
jumped 7.3% in the afternoon session after BMO Capital upgraded the stock to Outperform amid strong interest in its 3.2-terabit optical chipset for artificial intelligence data center infrastructure.
At European Microwave Week, the company also highlighted its portfolio of radio frequency and microwave products as reported by TipRanks.

Optical chipsets provide high-speed data transmission required to connect computing hardware within artificial intelligence data centers. The market responded to the product showcase at the industry conference alongside strong attention on high-performance networking components. These technology presentations and the positive reception to the company's optical hardware contributed to the rise in the share price.
What Is The Market Telling Us

MACOM’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 42 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock gained 5.9% on the news that weaker-than-expected U.S. employment data cooled Treasury yields, easing interest rate pressure. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 in September, falling short of the 84,000 projected by economists polled by Dow Jones, while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%.

For the broader group, softer hiring eases interest-rate pressure on high-multiple growth equities by pulling borrowing costs lower. However, further deceleration in the labor market risks dampening cyclical end-market demand across industrial and automotive chip channels.
Semiconductor valuations expand when falling yields reduce the discount rate on long-duration earnings, provided enterprise infrastructure spending does not deteriorate.

MACOM is up 100% since the beginning of the year, but at $350.51 per share, it is still trading 14.4% below its 52-week high of $409.68 from May 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of MACOM’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $5,375.
